xAI has released Grok 4.7, the latest version of its Grok family of AI models, featuring enhanced multimodal capabilities and significantly reduced pricing. The release continues xAI's rapid iteration pace under Elon Musk's leadership.

## Multimodal Advancements

Grok 4.7 introduces improved image understanding and reasoning capabilities, building on the multimodal foundation established in Grok 4.5. The model maintains a 500,000 token context window and adds support for more complex visual reasoning tasks.

The model is now available through xAI's API at $1.60 per million input tokens and $4.80 per million output tokens, representing a substantial reduction from previous pricing. Batch processing further reduces costs to $0.80/$2.40 per million tokens.

## xAI's Market Position

The release positions xAI as a more aggressive competitor in the AI market, directly challenging OpenAI and Anthropic on both capability and price. Grok 4.7's pricing undercuts many competing models while offering competitive performance on reasoning benchmarks.

xAI has been expanding its infrastructure rapidly, with new data centers coming online to support the computational demands of training and serving frontier models. The company recently announced partnerships with multiple cloud providers to scale its API availability.

## Growing AI Competition

Grok 4.7 joins what has become a crowded field of September 2026 releases, with OpenAI's GPT-6 family, Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5, and Xiaomi's MiMo V2.6 all launching within days of each other. This rapid release cadence reflects the intensely competitive AI landscape, where model differentiation increasingly hinges on specialized capabilities and pricing.

The release also comes amid ongoing controversy, with xAI and other AI labs facing an antitrust lawsuit alleging coordination to slow AI development—a claim the companies have denied.
